summary: No new receipt this turn, so I tightened the account's causal claim and its presentation. The rationale now explains why the concurrent-leader and truncation outcome belongs to the stale base rather than to the partition itself: with a correct configuration the same partition cannot commit the change at all, because the change installs its own membership into the commitment and that membership still contains the partitioned voter, so its quorum is unreachable (the four-voter case needs three of four) — whereas the stale base both shrinks the base the change is computed from and substitutes a voter, letting A plus one acknowledger meet the new quorum while the partitioned voter stays out, exactly as the dual-majority receipts show and as the control mode's refusal under the committed membership illustrates. I also consolidated the two process-traceability notes about the earlier build failure into a single, clearly historical item, keeping the concrete detail (which revision failed, which correction superseded it, and that the failed receipt carries no evidence) without duplicating it.
